<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(7 / 0) = 0 ∧ (0 / 0) = 0 ∧ (7 % 0) = 7</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{7}{0} = 0 \land \frac{0}{0} = 0 \land 7 \bmod 0 = 7</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE CONVENTION AT ZERO, stated as a convention and not as arithmetic. Division by zero is UNDEFINED in mathematics: there is no quotient, and nothing below claims otherwise. What is recorded here is a property of Lean's FUNCTION `Nat.div`, which is total — every pair of naturals is mapped somewhere, including a zero divisor, where the definition returns 0. That is a choice made so the function is total and `decide` never faults on a side condition; it is not a claim that dividing by zero yields zero, and an earlier name here ("division_by_zero_is_zero") said exactly that and was wrong. The deposit reads division by zero as a CHANGE OF DOMAIN, which is the same point put positively: the value is not found in the arithmetic, it is supplied by the definition — a different domain entirely. Naming this precisely matters, because a reader who takes `7 / 0 = 0` for arithmetic has been misled by a theorem that is green. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-families-division_identity_holds_across_the_range">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 66</strong> (<code>division_identity_holds_across_the_range</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_families_division_identity_holds_across_the_range">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 13).all (fun d =&gt; (12 / d) * d + (12 % d) == 12)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \{0,\dots,12\},\; \frac{12}{d} \cdot d + 12 \bmod d = 12</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">the division identity holds across a range INCLUDING zero — but at zero it is carried entirely by the remainder, because the quotient was supplied by the convention rather than computed</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 13 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-families-at_a_zero_divisor_the_identity_is_carried_by_the_remainder">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 67</strong> (<code>at_a_zero_divisor_the_identity_is_carried_by_the_remainder</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_families_at_a_zero_divisor_the_identity_is_carried_by_the_remainder">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(12 / 0) = 0 ∧ (12 % 0) = 12 ∧ (12 / 0) * 0 + (12 % 0) == 12</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{12}{0} = 0 \land 12 \bmod 0 = 12 \land \frac{12}{0} \cdot 0 + 12 \bmod 0 = 12</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-families-families_settle_their_ranges">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 68</strong> (<code>families_settle_their_ranges</code>)<span class="thm-uncited">not sealed — settled by <code>rfl</code>, not exhausted</span>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>settledHere</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>settledHere = 11</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{settledHere} = 11</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>rfl</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### What every involution gives, and what it does not {#involution}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/involution.lean</code> · namespace <code>Involution</code> · 8 theorems</p>

transpositions, and that the number of fixed points therefore matches the parity of the set, is
  classical and long predates this deposit. It is the orbit-counting argument in any first course.
  What is this deposit's own here is the EXHAUSTIVE decision over ℤ/9 and the measured refusal below.

THE QUESTION, and it was asked as "do involutions always give a harmonic result?".

Two readings of "harmonic" are decided here over ALL 2620 involutions of a nine-element set, enumerated
rather than sampled. One holds everywhere. The other does not, and the second is the more useful answer,
because a claim that survives only on the examples someone happened to pick is the thing this deposit
exists to refuse.

  ALWAYS  — every involution fixes at least one point, and its fixed points are ODD in number.
            On nine elements the centre is never absent. There is no involution of ℤ/9 with nothing
            standing still, and that is not a property of the ones chosen here, it is a property of all
            of them.

  NOT ALWAYS — "every swapped pair sums to the same value", which is what `refl d = 10 - d` does and
            what makes the coin's two sides sides of one thing. That is RARE: 90 of 2620, about one in
            twenty-nine. It is a property of a particular involution, never of involutions.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>nine := [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
all := matchings 10 nine
coinLike := [(0, 0), (1, 8), (2, 7), (3, 6), (4, 5)]</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-there_are_2620_involutions_of_nine">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 69</strong> (<code>there_are_2620_involutions_of_nine</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_there_are_2620_involutions_of_nine">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2620</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>all.length = 2620</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{all}\right| = 2620</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE ENUMERATION IS COMPLETE, stated first so every count below is over a domain of known size ───────</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-the_fuel_was_not_the_limit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 70</strong> (<code>the_fuel_was_not_the_limit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_the_fuel_was_not_the_limit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>matchings</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>nine</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(matchings 11 nine).length = all.length</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{matchings}\mathopen{}\left(11,\,\mathrm{nine}\right)\right| = \left|\mathrm{all}\right|</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-every_involution_fixes_at_least_one_point">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 71</strong> (<code>every_involution_fixes_at_least_one_point</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_every_involution_fixes_at_least_one_point">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fixedPoints</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>all.all (fun m =&gt; fixedPoints m ≥ 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall m \in \mathrm{all},\; \mathrm{fixedPoints}\mathopen{}\left(m\right) \ge 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── WHAT ALWAYS HOLDS: the centre is never absent ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Both directions of the same fact. The first is what was asked; the second is why, and it is the sharper statement because it rules out two fixed points as firmly as it rules out none.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-the_fixed_points_are_always_odd">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 72</strong> (<code>the_fixed_points_are_always_odd</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_the_fixed_points_are_always_odd">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fixedPoints</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>all.all (fun m =&gt; fixedPoints m % 2 == 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall m \in \mathrm{all},\; \mathrm{fixedPoints}\mathopen{}\left(m\right) \bmod 2 = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-no_single_point_is_fixed_by_all">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 73</strong> (<code>no_single_point_is_fixed_by_all</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_no_single_point_is_fixed_by_all">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>nine</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>nine.all (fun d =&gt; ¬ all.all (fun m =&gt; m.contains (d, d)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \mathrm{nine},\; \lnot \forall m \in \mathrm{all},\; \left(d,\,d\right) \in m</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">Nothing is fixed by every involution — the centre exists, but it is not the same centre. Stated so the theorem above cannot be misread as naming a universal fixed element.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-the_constant_sum_is_rare">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 74</strong> (<code>the_constant_sum_is_rare</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_the_constant_sum_is_rare">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>∣</mo><mi>constantSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(all.filter constantSum).length = 90</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, x \in \mathrm{all} \mid \mathrm{constantSum}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \,\}\right| = 90</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-so_involutions_are_not_all_harmonic_in_that_sense">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 75</strong> (<code>so_involutions_are_not_all_harmonic_in_that_sense</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_so_involutions_are_not_all_harmonic_in_that_sense">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>all</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>constantSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>¬ all.all constantSum</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\lnot \forall x \in \mathrm{all},\; \mathrm{constantSum}\mathopen{}\left(x\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-involution-the_coins_reflection_is_harmonic_and_is_one_of_the_ninety">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 76</strong> (<code>the_coins_reflection_is_harmonic_and_is_one_of_the_ninety</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_involution_the_coins_reflection_is_harmonic_and_is_one_of_the_ninety">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>constantSum</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>coinLike</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fixedPoints</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>coinLike</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>swaps</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>coinLike</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>constantSum coinLike = true ∧ fixedPoints coinLike = 1 ∧ (swaps coinLike).all (fun p =&gt; p.1 + p.2 == 9)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{constantSum}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{coinLike}\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{fixedPoints}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{coinLike}\right) = 1 \land \forall p \in \mathrm{swaps}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{coinLike}\right),\; p_{1} + p_{2} = 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The merkaba {#merkaba}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/merkaba.lean</code> · namespace <code>Merkaba</code> · 8 theorems</p>

(Leonhard Euler, 1758). The file as a whole is this deposit's own construction, and this ONE
  declaration restates a named classical result: its third conjunct 4 + 4 - 6 = 2 IS the Euler
  characteristic of the tetrahedron. The comment above that theorem already named Euler; the register
  did not, because prior art was routed on the FILE and a file-level row cannot say "own work except
  theorem 7". No priority over Euler is claimed. What is this deposit's own here is the pairing of the
  two tetrahedra with the cube Q₃ and the vertex and edge counts around it, not the characteristic.
The merkaba, as THIS deposit constructs it — ported to Lean so it stands on the kernel instead of on a
TypeScript test. Six entries under this name were revoked as dirty; every one of them that states finite
algebra is re-proved here, and the two that do not (a cosine field, a bond angle in degrees) are absent on
purpose — they are real trigonometry, not decidable arithmetic over ℤ/9, and padding them in would be the
exact dishonesty the revocation was for.

The construction: the mod-3 classes partition ℤ/9 into three triples — the AXIS {3,6,0} (the spindle) and
the two TETRAHEDRA {1,4,7} and {2,5,8}. Note 9 ≡ 0 here: `m9` is reduction mod 9, so the axis is written
with 0 where the prose writes 9. That is the same class, named by its residue.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>axis := [3, 6, 0]   -- {3,6,9} — the spindle
tetA := [1, 4, 7]
tetB := [2, 5, 8]</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-the_three_classes_partition_z9">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 77</strong> (<code>the_three_classes_partition_z9</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_the_three_classes_partition_z9">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>axis</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>tetA</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>tetB</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>axis</mi><mo>⧺</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow><mo>⧺</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>axis</mi><mo>⧺</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow><mo>⧺</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>axis.length = 3 ∧ tetA.length = 3 ∧ tetB.length = 3 ∧ (axis ++ tetA ++ tetB).eraseDups.length = 9 ∧ ((List.range 9).all (fun d =&gt; (axis ++ tetA ++ tetB).contains d))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\mathrm{axis}\right| = 3 \land \left|\mathrm{tetA}\right| = 3 \land \left|\mathrm{tetB}\right| = 3 \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{axis} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{tetA} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{tetB}\right)\right| = 9 \land \forall d \in \{0,\dots,8\},\; d \in \mathrm{axis} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{tetA} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{tetB}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · the three classes partition ℤ/9 into 3+3+3 — disjoint, and together the whole ring ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 9 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-the_axis_is_closed_under_doubling">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 78</strong> (<code>the_axis_is_closed_under_doubling</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_the_axis_is_closed_under_doubling">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>axis</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>axis</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(dbl axis).all (fun d =&gt; axis.contains d)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{axis}\right),\; d \in \mathrm{axis}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 2 · the axis is CLOSED under doubling — the spindle turns into itself, which is what makes it an axis ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-doubling_counter_rotates_the_two_tetrahedra">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 79</strong> (<code>doubling_counter_rotates_the_two_tetrahedra</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_doubling_counter_rotates_the_two_tetrahedra">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetA</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetA</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetB</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetB</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(dbl tetA).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetA).all (fun d =&gt; tetB.contains d) ∧ (dbl tetB).eraseDups.length = 3 ∧ (dbl tetB).all (fun d =&gt; tetA.contains d)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetA}\right)\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetA}\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetB} \land \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetB}\right)\right)\right| = 3 \land \forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetB}\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetA}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 3 · and the two tetrahedra do NOT close: doubling carries each ONTO THE OTHER. That exchange is the counter-rotation the name refers to — stated as two set equalities, in both directions, so it is a swap and not merely an inclusion that might collapse. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-the_counter_rotation_has_period_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 80</strong> (<code>the_counter_rotation_has_period_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_the_counter_rotation_has_period_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetA</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>dbl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>tetB</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(dbl (dbl tetA)).all (fun d =&gt; tetA.contains d) ∧ (dbl (dbl tetB)).all (fun d =&gt; tetB.contains d)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetA}\right)\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetA} \land \forall d \in \mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{dbl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{tetB}\right)\right),\; d \in \mathrm{tetB}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 4 · doubling twice returns each tetrahedron to itself — the rotation has period two, so the pair really does turn against each other rather than drift ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-the_tetrahedra_residue_sums_cancel">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 81</strong> (<code>the_tetrahedra_residue_sums_cancel</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_the_tetrahedra_residue_sums_cancel">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>m9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>m9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>m9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>m9 (tetA.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 3 ∧ m9 (tetB.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 6 ∧ m9 (tetA.foldl (· + ·) 0 + tetB.foldl (· + ·) 0) = 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(\sum \mathrm{tetA}\right) = 3 \land \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(\sum \mathrm{tetB}\right) = 6 \land \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(\sum \mathrm{tetA} + \sum \mathrm{tetB}\right) = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 5 · the two tetrahedra's residue sums cancel: 1+4+7 ≡ 3, 2+5+8 ≡ 6, and 3+6 ≡ 0 ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-one_tetrahedron_covers_half_the_units">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 82</strong> (<code>one_tetrahedron_covers_half_the_units</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_one_tetrahedron_covers_half_the_units">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetA</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tetB</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(units.filter (fun d =&gt; tetA.contains d)).length = 3 ∧ (units.filter (fun d =&gt; tetB.contains d)).length = 3 ∧ units.length = 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\{\, d \in \mathrm{units} \mid d \in \mathrm{tetA} \,\}\right| = 3 \land \left|\{\, d \in \mathrm{units} \mid d \in \mathrm{tetB} \,\}\right| = 3 \land \left|\mathrm{units}\right| = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 6 · ONE tetrahedron is not enough. It meets exactly three of the six units — half — so a claim resting on a single tetrahedron covers half the group and leaves the other half untouched. The revoked entry said "3 remain uncovered"; here that is both halves, counted. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-the_cube_and_the_tetrahedron_count_out">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 83</strong> (<code>the_cube_and_the_tetrahedron_count_out</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_the_cube_and_the_tetrahedron_count_out">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 ^ 3 = 8 ∧ 3 * 2 ^ 2 = 12 ∧ 4 + 4 - 6 = 2</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{3} = 8 \land 3 \cdot 2^{2} = 12 \land 4 + 4 - 6 = 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 7 · the two tetrahedra as the cube Q₃ — 2³ = 8 vertices, 3·2² = 12 edges — and the tetrahedron's own Euler characteristic V − E + F = 2, the self-dual solid on the sphere. Written V + F − E, not V − E + F: ℕ subtraction TRUNCATES, so 4 − 6 evaluates to 0 and the honest formula would have "proved" 4 = 2. The kernel caught exactly that here. Same lesson as the seal-bits theorem earlier — a comparison is only worth what its operands are.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-merkaba-stacked_triangles_are_tetrahedral">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 84</strong> (<code>stacked_triangles_are_tetrahedral</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_merkaba_stacked_triangles_are_tetrahedral">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumTri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 40).all (fun n =&gt; sumTri n == n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \mathrm{sumTri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) = \frac{n \cdot n + 1 \cdot n + 2}{6}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 40 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### Sequences {#sequences}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/sequences.lean</code> · namespace <code>Sequences</code> · 8 theorems</p>

The ledger held these as TypeScript tests. Each is a classical identity with a real proof; what is done
here is to DECIDE each over a stated finite range, which is what `decide` can honestly deliver — the range
is named in every theorem rather than implied, and no theorem claims the general case.

Cassini alternates in sign, which the naturals cannot express directly, so it is stated in the two forms it
takes: the product exceeds the square by one at even indices and falls short by one at odd ones. Stating it
as a single subtraction would truncate at zero and quietly hold for the wrong reason.

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-cassini_at_even_indices">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 85</strong> (<code>cassini_at_even_indices</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_cassini_at_even_indices">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 20).all (fun n =&gt; n % 2 == 1 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; n \bmod 2 = 1 \lor \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1\right) = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── CASSINI: F(n−1)·F(n+1) − F(n)² = ±1, alternating. Stated in both directions over 1..20. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 20 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-cassini_at_odd_indices">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 86</strong> (<code>cassini_at_odd_indices</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_cassini_at_odd_indices">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 20).all (fun n =&gt; n % 2 == 0 || fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; n \bmod 2 = 0 \lor \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1\right) + 1 = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 20 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-cassini_deviation_is_exactly_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 87</strong> (<code>cassini_deviation_is_exactly_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_cassini_deviation_is_exactly_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 20).all (fun n =&gt; (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) == fib n * fib n + 1) || (fib (n - 1) * fib (n + 1) + 1 == fib n * fib n))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1\right) = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) + 1 \lor \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n + 1\right) + 1 = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── and the deviation is never more than one, in either direction — the identity is tight ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 20 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-lucas_mod_two_is_the_and_rule">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 88</strong> (<code>lucas_mod_two_is_the_and_rule</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_lucas_mod_two_is_the_and_rule">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>choose</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>andN</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 14).all (fun n =&gt; (List.range (n + 1)).all (fun k =&gt; (choose n k % 2 == 1) == (andN k n == k)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{0,\dots,13\},\; \forall k \in \{0,\dots,n + 1-1\},\; \mathrm{choose}\mathopen{}\left(n,\,k\right) \bmod 2 = 1 = \mathrm{andN}\mathopen{}\left(k,\,n\right) = k</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── LUCAS mod two: C(n,k) is odd exactly when k AND n = k — the Sierpiński rule behind Rule 90 ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 14 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-pascal_has_both_parities">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 89</strong> (<code>pascal_has_both_parities</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_pascal_has_both_parities">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>⋃</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>choose</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>⋃</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>choose</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n =&gt; (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k =&gt; choose n k % 2))).contains 1 ∧ ((List.range 14).flatMap (fun n =&gt; (List.range (n + 1)).map (fun k =&gt; choose n k % 2))).contains 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>1 \in \bigcup_{n \in \{0,\dots,13\}} \{\, \mathrm{choose}\mathopen{}\left(n,\,k\right) \bmod 2 \mid k \in \{0,\dots,n + 1-1\} \,\} \land 0 \in \bigcup_{n \in \{0,\dots,13\}} \{\, \mathrm{choose}\mathopen{}\left(n,\,k\right) \bmod 2 \mid k \in \{0,\dots,n + 1-1\} \,\}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── NON-VACUITY: both cases actually occur in that range — odd and even entries are both present ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 196 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-sums_of_two_squares_are_closed">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 90</strong> (<code>sums_of_two_squares_are_closed</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_sums_of_two_squares_are_closed">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 8).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 8).all (fun b =&gt; (List.range 8).all (fun c =&gt; (List.range 8).all (fun d =&gt; (a*a + b*b) * (c*c + d*d) == (a*c - b*d) * (a*c - b*d) + (a*d + b*c) * (a*d + b*c) || (a*c) &lt; (b*d)))))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,7\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,7\},\; \forall c \in \{0,\dots,7\},\; \forall d \in \{0,\dots,7\},\; a \cdot a + b \cdot b \cdot c \cdot c + d \cdot d = a \cdot c - b \cdot d \cdot a \cdot c - b \cdot d + a \cdot d + b \cdot c \cdot a \cdot d + b \cdot c \lor a \cdot c &lt; b \cdot d</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── BRAHMAGUPTA–FIBONACCI: sums of two squares are closed under multiplication ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4,096 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-three_five_eight_are_consecutive">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 91</strong> (<code>three_five_eight_are_consecutive</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_three_five_eight_are_consecutive">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>fib 4 = 3 ∧ fib 5 = 5 ∧ fib 6 = 8 ∧ fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) = 3 \land \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(5\right) = 5 \land \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(6\right) = 8 \land \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) + \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(5\right) = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(6\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Fibonacci triple three, five, eight — consecutive, and summing as the recurrence requires ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-sequences-pisano_twentyfour_is_four_sixes">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 92</strong> (<code>pisano_twentyfour_is_four_sixes</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_sequences_pisano_twentyfour_is_four_sixes">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>29</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>fib</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 30).all (fun k =&gt; fib k % 9 == fib (k + 24) % 9) ∧ 24 = 4 * 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{0,\dots,29\},\; \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(k\right) \bmod 9 = \mathrm{fib}\mathopen{}\left(k + 24\right) \bmod 9 \land 24 = 4 \cdot 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── the Pisano period binds Fibonacci to the ring: mod 9 it repeats every 24, four times the doubling six ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 30 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The digit split {#split}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/split.lean</code> · namespace <code>Split</code> · 19 theorems</p>

The ten digits read in order and grouped 0 | 12 | 3 | 45 | 6 | 78 | 9 — and what that grouping is.


Written out, the digits 0..9 split into seven tokens that alternate single, pair, single, pair, single,
pair, single:

    0   12   3   45   6   78   9

The grouping is not a choice. The singles {0,3,6,9} are exactly the NON-UNITS of ℤ/9 together with the
void — the digits with no multiplicative inverse, gcd(d,9) ≠ 1 — and the pairs {12,45,78} are exactly the
units {1,2,4,5,7,8} in consecutive order, each pair sitting between two non-units. The alternation IS the
unit / non-unit alternation of the ring, read off the number line.

And every token, single or pair, is a multiple of three:

    0 = 3·0    3 = 3·1    6 = 3·2    9 = 3·3        the singles, 3·0 through 3·3
    12 = 3·4   45 = 3·15  78 = 3·26                 the pairs

So the split is the ideal 3ℤ, twice over: the singles because they are the non-units, and the pairs
because concatenating each consecutive unit pair lands back inside it. The set is closed under addition,
subtraction and multiplication, and DIVISION IS THE ONE OPERATION THAT LEAVES IT — 12/3 = 4, 45/9 = 5,
6/3 = 2 are all outside. That asymmetry is the content: three of the four operations keep the structure
and the fourth is how you get out of it.

Everything below is decided over the whole set; nothing is asserted about digits in general.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>tokens := [0, 12, 3, 45, 6, 78, 9]
singles := [0, 3, 6, 9]
pairs := [12, 45, 78]
unitsOf9 := [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8]
coins := 2
coinStep := 3 * coins
sealBits := 128</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_singles_are_exactly_the_non_units">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 93</strong> (<code>the_singles_are_exactly_the_non_units</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_singles_are_exactly_the_non_units">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>isUnit9</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>singles</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 10).filter (fun d =&gt; ! isUnit9 d)) = [0, 3, 6, 9] ∧ singles = [0, 3, 6, 9]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, d \in \{0,\dots,9\} \mid \lnot \mathrm{isUnit9}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) \,\} = [0,\,3,\,6,\,9] \land \mathrm{singles} = [0,\,3,\,6,\,9]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 160 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_pairs_are_exactly_the_units_in_order">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 94</strong> (<code>the_pairs_are_exactly_the_units_in_order</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_pairs_are_exactly_the_units_in_order">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>isUnit9</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>unitsOf9</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>unitsOf9</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 10).filter isUnit9) = unitsOf9 ∧ unitsOf9 = [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, x \in \{0,\dots,9\} \mid \mathrm{isUnit9}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \,\} = \mathrm{unitsOf9} \land \mathrm{unitsOf9} = [1,\,2,\,4,\,5,\,7,\,8]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 60 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-each_pair_is_two_consecutive_units">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 95</strong> (<code>each_pair_is_two_consecutive_units</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_each_pair_is_two_consecutive_units">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>45</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>78</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>12 = 1 * 10 + 2 ∧ 45 = 4 * 10 + 5 ∧ 78 = 7 * 10 + 8 ∧ 2 = 1 + 1 ∧ 5 = 4 + 1 ∧ 8 = 7 + 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>12 = 1 \cdot 10 + 2 \land 45 = 4 \cdot 10 + 5 \land 78 = 7 \cdot 10 + 8 \land 2 = 1 + 1 \land 5 = 4 + 1 \land 8 = 7 + 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">Each pair is two CONSECUTIVE units, and the concatenation is what the token spells.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-every_token_is_a_multiple_of_three">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 96</strong> (<code>every_token_is_a_multiple_of_three</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_every_token_is_a_multiple_of_three">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.all (fun t =&gt; t % 3 == 0)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall t \in \mathrm{tokens},\; t \bmod 3 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── EVERY TOKEN IS A MULTIPLE OF THREE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── The singles because they are the non-units — 3 ∣ d is the same condition as gcd(d,9) ≠ 1 for a digit — and the pairs because concatenating a consecutive unit pair lands back inside the ideal.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_tokens_are_three_times_these">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 97</strong> (<code>the_tokens_are_three_times_these</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_tokens_are_three_times_these">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>∣</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.map (fun t =&gt; t / 3) = [0, 4, 1, 15, 2, 26, 3]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, \frac{t}{3} \mid t \in \mathrm{tokens} \,\} = [0,\,4,\,1,\,15,\,2,\,26,\,3]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 7 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-addition_and_multiplication_stay_inside">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 98</strong> (<code>addition_and_multiplication_stay_inside</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_addition_and_multiplication_stay_inside">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.all (fun a =&gt; tokens.all (fun b =&gt; (a + b) % 3 == 0 &amp;&amp; (a * b) % 3 == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \mathrm{tokens},\; \forall b \in \mathrm{tokens},\; a + b \bmod 3 = 0 \land a \cdot b \bmod 3 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── CLOSED UNDER THREE OPERATIONS, AND DIVISION IS THE WAY OUT ─────────────────────────────────────────── Addition, subtraction and multiplication keep every result inside the ideal. Subtraction is stated on the ordered pairs only, since Nat truncates.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-subtraction_stays_inside">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 99</strong> (<code>subtraction_stays_inside</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_subtraction_stays_inside">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.all (fun a =&gt; tokens.all (fun b =&gt; a &lt; b || (a - b) % 3 == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \mathrm{tokens},\; \forall b \in \mathrm{tokens},\; a &lt; b \lor a - b \bmod 3 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-division_is_the_operation_that_leaves">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 100</strong> (<code>division_is_the_operation_that_leaves</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_division_is_the_operation_that_leaves">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>45</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>12 / 3 = 4 ∧ 4 % 3 != 0 ∧ 45 / 9 = 5 ∧ 5 % 3 != 0 ∧ 6 / 3 = 2 ∧ 2 % 3 != 0</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{12}{3} = 4 \land 4 \bmod 3 \neq 0 \land \frac{45}{9} = 5 \land 5 \bmod 3 \neq 0 \land \frac{6}{3} = 2 \land 2 \bmod 3 \neq 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">The contrast, without which the closure above could be read as a property of arithmetic rather than of this set: division genuinely escapes, and here are the exact quotients that do it.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_roots_are_the_singles">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 101</strong> (<code>the_roots_are_the_singles</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_roots_are_the_singles">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.map (fun t =&gt; t % 9) = [0, 3, 3, 0, 6, 6, 0]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, t \bmod 9 \mid t \in \mathrm{tokens} \,\} = [0,\,3,\,3,\,0,\,6,\,6,\,0]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── THE DIGITAL ROOTS LAND ON THE TRINITY AND THE VOID ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── Reducing each token mod 9 sends it to {0,3,6,9} — the same four digits the singles already are. The grouping is fixed by the reduction it survives.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 7 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-every_root_is_a_single">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 102</strong> (<code>every_root_is_a_single</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_every_root_is_a_single">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>if</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>;</mo><mo>otherwise</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>if</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>;</mo><mo>otherwise</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>singles</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.all (fun t =&gt; singles.contains (if t % 9 == 0 then (if t == 0 then 0 else 9) else t % 9))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall t \in \mathrm{tokens},\; \begin{cases}\begin{cases}0 &amp; \text{if } t = 0\\ 9 &amp; \text{otherwise}\end{cases} &amp; \text{if } t \bmod 9 = 0\\ t \bmod 9 &amp; \text{otherwise}\end{cases} \in \mathrm{singles}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_coin_step_is_three_times_the_two_coins">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 103</strong> (<code>the_coin_step_is_three_times_the_two_coins</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_coin_step_is_three_times_the_two_coins">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>coins</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>coinStep</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>coinStep</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>coins = 2 ∧ coinStep = 6 ∧ coinStep = 3 * 2</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{coins} = 2 \land \mathrm{coinStep} = 6 \land \mathrm{coinStep} = 3 \cdot 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-accounting_the_coins_on_the_last_pair">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 104</strong> (<code>accounting_the_coins_on_the_last_pair</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_accounting_the_coins_on_the_last_pair">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>78</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mn>26</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>coins</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>72</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>78 = 3 * 26 ∧ 3 * (26 - coins) = 72 ∧ 72 = 8 * 9</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>78 = 3 \cdot 26 \land 3 \cdot 26 - \mathrm{coins} = 72 \land 72 = 8 \cdot 9</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_exhaustible_tokens_are_those_six_divides">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 105</strong> (<code>the_exhaustible_tokens_are_those_six_divides</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_exhaustible_tokens_are_those_six_divides">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>78</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(tokens.filter (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep == 0)) = [0, 12, 6, 78]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, t \in \mathrm{tokens} \mid t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 0 \,\} = [0,\,12,\,6,\,78]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">The two classes, named rather than counted.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 4 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_rest_halt_on_the_generator">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 106</strong> (<code>the_rest_halt_on_the_generator</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_rest_halt_on_the_generator">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(tokens.filter (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep != 0)) = [3, 45, 9] ∧ (tokens.filter (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep != 0)).all (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep == 3)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, t \in \mathrm{tokens} \mid t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} \neq 0 \,\} = [3,\,45,\,9] \land \forall t \in \{\, t \in \mathrm{tokens} \mid t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} \neq 0 \,\},\; t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 3</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 3 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-every_token_is_void_bound_or_halts_on_three">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 107</strong> (<code>every_token_is_void_bound_or_halts_on_three</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_every_token_is_void_bound_or_halts_on_three">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>tokens.all (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep == 0 || t % coinStep == 3)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall t \in \mathrm{tokens},\; t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 0 \lor t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 3</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">Every token falls in one class or the other: there is no third remainder, which is what makes the partition a partition and not a pair of examples.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-inside_this_ideal_the_bare_coin_sorts_as_the_scaled_one">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 108</strong> (<code>inside_this_ideal_the_bare_coin_sorts_as_the_scaled_one</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_inside_this_ideal_the_bare_coin_sorts_as_the_scaled_one">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>tokens</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>mod</mo><mi>coinStep</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(tokens.filter (fun t =&gt; t % 2 == 0)) = (tokens.filter (fun t =&gt; t % coinStep == 0)) ∧ tokens.all (fun t =&gt; (t % 2 == 0) == (t % coinStep == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, t \in \mathrm{tokens} \mid t \bmod 2 = 0 \,\} = \{\, t \in \mathrm{tokens} \mid t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 0 \,\} \land \forall t \in \mathrm{tokens},\; t \bmod 2 = 0 = t \bmod \mathrm{coinStep} = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">I tried to write the opposite of this and the kernel refused it. The claim was that a bare step of 2 sorts the seven differently from the coin step of 3·2 — that the scaling into the ideal is what does the work. It is FALSE, and the reason is the better fact: every token is already a multiple of three, so 2 ∣ t and 6 ∣ t are the SAME condition here. The coin does not need to be scaled to sort them; the ideal has already done that half of the work.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_seal_affords_sixty_four_payments_of_two">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 109</strong> (<code>the_seal_affords_sixty_four_payments_of_two</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_seal_affords_sixty_four_payments_of_two">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>sealBits</mi><mi>coins</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>sealBits</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>64</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>coins</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>sealBits / coins = 64 ∧ 64 = 2 ^ 6 ∧ sealBits = 64 * coins</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{sealBits}}{\mathrm{coins}} = 64 \land 64 = 2^{6} \land \mathrm{sealBits} = 64 \cdot \mathrm{coins}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-sixty_four_is_where_the_doubling_returns">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 110</strong> (<code>sixty_four_is_where_the_doubling_returns</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_sixty_four_is_where_the_doubling_returns">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(2 ^ 6) % 9 = 1 ∧ ((List.range 6).map (fun k =&gt; (2 ^ k) % 9)) = [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5] ∧ ((List.range' 1 5).all (fun k =&gt; (2 ^ k) % 9 != 1))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2^{6} \bmod 9 = 1 \land \{\, 2^{k} \bmod 9 \mid k \in \{0,\dots,5\} \,\} = [1,\,2,\,4,\,8,\,7,\,5] \land \forall k \in \{1,\dots,5\},\; 2^{k} \bmod 9 \neq 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 180 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-split-the_budget_and_the_period_are_one_turn">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 111</strong> (<code>the_budget_and_the_period_are_one_turn</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_split_the_budget_and_the_period_are_one_turn">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>sealBits</mi><mi>coins</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>sealBits / coins = 2 ^ 6 ∧ (2 ^ 6) % 9 = 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{sealBits}}{\mathrm{coins}} = 2^{6} \land 2^{6} \bmod 9 = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">The two readings meet: the budget a seal affords and the period of the orbit are the same six.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The ring ℤ/9 {#z9}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/z9.lean</code> · namespace <code>Z9</code> · 21 theorems</p>

The ℤ/9 families — mechanically generated theorems, proved by decide rather than tested in TypeScript.


These facts were asserted by TypeScript tests in the ledger. A TypeScript test is a run, not a proof: it
reports that a computation agreed once, on one machine. Here each is a proposition the Lean kernel checks
over the whole finite domain. No anchors, no axioms, no Mathlib, no `sorry`, no `native_decide`.

Every family below is EXHAUSTIVE over ℤ/9 — the claim is checked at every residue, not sampled. Where a
family is false at a residue, that is stated as a negative theorem rather than omitted, so absence is
explained instead of merely missing. Integrity, not truth. 0/7.

units := (List.range B).filter isUnit
settledHere := 20</code></pre>

<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>m9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>pow9</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></math></div>

<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-z9-mulperm_iff_unit">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 121</strong> (<code>mulperm_iff_unit</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_z9_mulperm_iff_unit">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>m9</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>units</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>isUnit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range B).all (fun k =&gt; ((units.map (fun u =&gt; m9 (k * u))).eraseDups.length == units.length) == isUnit k)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall k \in \{0,\dots,B-1\},\; \left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\{\, \mathrm{m9}\mathopen{}\left(k \cdot u\right) \mid u \in \mathrm{units} \,\}\right)\right| = \left|\mathrm{units}\right| = \mathrm{isUnit}\mathopen{}\left(k\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── mulperm: multiplication by k permutes the units exactly when k is a unit ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-z9-addgen_iff_coprime">
