<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>tri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>tri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>isSquareBelow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>900</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isSquareBelow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>900</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 40).all (fun n =&gt; sumPow 3 n == tri n * tri n) ∧ (List.range' 1 40).all (fun n =&gt; sumPow 3 n == sumPow 1 n * sumPow 1 n) ∧ (List.range' 2 19).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ isSquareBelow 900 (sumPow 4 n)) ∧ isSquareBelow 900 (sumPow 4 1) = true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,n\right) = \mathrm{tri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{tri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \land \forall n \in \{1,\dots,40\},\; \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(3,\,n\right) = \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,n\right) \cdot \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,n\right) \land \forall n \in \{2,\dots,20\},\; \lnot \mathrm{isSquareBelow}\mathopen{}\left(900,\,\mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(4,\,n\right)\right) \land \mathrm{isSquareBelow}\mathopen{}\left(900,\,\mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(4,\,1\right)\right) = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 30,400 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-picks_theorem_holds_for_every_lattice_triangle_in_the_four_grid">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 174</strong> (<code>picks_theorem_holds_for_every_lattice_triangle_in_the_four_grid</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_picks_theorem_holds_for_every_lattice_triangle_in_the_four_grid">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>interiorCount</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>boundaryCount</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>:</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>:</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pts</mi><mo>:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>interiorCount</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>boundaryCount</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>triples</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1548</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>triples</mi><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cross</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>interiorCount</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>516</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>pts.all (fun a =&gt; pts.all (fun b =&gt; pts.all (fun c =&gt; cross a b c ≤ 0 || cross a b c == 2 * interiorCount a b c + boundaryCount a b c - 2))) ∧ ¬ pts.any (fun a =&gt; pts.any (fun b =&gt; pts.any (fun c =&gt; cross a b c &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; cross a b c == 2 * interiorCount a b c + boundaryCount a b c))) ∧ (triples.filter (fun t =&gt; cross t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 &gt; 0)).length = 1548 ∧ (triples.filter (fun t =&gt; cross t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; interiorCount t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2 &gt; 0)).length = 516</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \mathrm{pts},\; \forall b \in \mathrm{pts},\; \forall c \in \mathrm{pts},\; \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) \le 0 \lor \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) = 2 \cdot \mathrm{interiorCount}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) + \mathrm{boundaryCount}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) - 2 \land \lnot \exists a \in \mathrm{pts} : \exists b \in \mathrm{pts} : \exists c \in \mathrm{pts} : \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) &gt; 0 \land \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) = 2 \cdot \mathrm{interiorCount}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) + \mathrm{boundaryCount}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) \land \left|\{\, t \in \mathrm{triples} \mid \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(t_{1},\,t_{2}_{1},\,t_{2}_{2}\right) &gt; 0 \,\}\right| = 1548 \land \left|\{\, t \in \mathrm{triples} \mid \mathrm{cross}\mathopen{}\left(t_{1},\,t_{2}_{1},\,t_{2}_{2}\right) &gt; 0 \land \mathrm{interiorCount}\mathopen{}\left(t_{1},\,t_{2}_{1},\,t_{2}_{2}\right) &gt; 0 \,\}\right| = 516</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-bezouts_identity_is_attained_and_no_smaller_combination_exists">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 175</strong> (<code>bezouts_identity_is_attained_and_no_smaller_combination_exists</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_bezouts_identity_is_attained_and_no_smaller_combination_exists">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mo>∃</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>Families.gcd'</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mrow><mi>Families.gcd'</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Families.gcd'</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>240</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>46</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>47</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>240</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 30).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range' 1 30).all (fun b =&gt; (List.range 31).any (fun x =&gt; (List.range 31).any (fun y =&gt; a * x == b * y + Families.gcd' a b)))) ∧ (List.range' 1 20).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range' 1 20).all (fun b =&gt; (List.range 21).all (fun x =&gt; (List.range 21).all (fun y =&gt; a * x &lt; b * y || (a * x - b * y) % Families.gcd' a b == 0)))) ∧ Families.gcd' 240 46 = 2 ∧ 46 * 47 = 240 * 9 + 2</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{1,\dots,30\},\; \forall b \in \{1,\dots,30\},\; \exists x \in \{0,\dots,30\} : \exists y \in \{0,\dots,30\} : a \cdot x = b \cdot y + \mathrm{Families.gcd'}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) \land \forall a \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; \forall b \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; \forall x \in \{0,\dots,20\},\; \forall y \in \{0,\dots,20\},\; a \cdot x &lt; b \cdot y \lor a \cdot x - b \cdot y \bmod \mathrm{Families.gcd'}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{Families.gcd'}\mathopen{}\left(240,\,46\right) = 2 \land 46 \cdot 47 = 240 \cdot 9 + 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 3 · Bézout's identity — 6 impressions across three phrasings. Both halves of the statement are decided, because only together do they say that gcd is the LEAST positive combination rather than merely SOME combination. Attainment: for every pair of a, b up to 30 there are coefficients under 31 with a·x = b·y + gcd(a,b). Minimality: for every a, b, x, y up to 20, whenever a·x ≥ b·y the difference is a multiple of gcd(a,b) — so nothing smaller and positive is ever reachable. The subtraction is guarded by the inequality rather than performed, since ℕ subtraction truncates and a truncated 0 would satisfy the divisibility test for the wrong reason. The named instance is the textbook one: gcd(240, 46) = 2 attained as 46·47 − 240·9. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 152,568,360,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-the_latin_squares_of_order_four_number_five_hundred_and_seventy_six">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 176</strong> (<code>the_latin_squares_of_order_four_number_five_hundred_and_seventy_six</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_the_latin_squares_of_order_four_number_five_hundred_and_seventy_six">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>latinSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>576</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>latinSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>latinSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>latinSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>latinSquares</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>latinSquares 4 = 576 ∧ latinSquares 3 = 12 ∧ latinSquares 2 = 2 ∧ latinSquares 1 = 1 ∧ ¬ (latinSquares 4 = 24 * 24 * 24)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{latinSquares}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) = 576 \land \mathrm{latinSquares}\mathopen{}\left(3\right) = 12 \land \mathrm{latinSquares}\mathopen{}\left(2\right) = 2 \land \mathrm{latinSquares}\mathopen{}\left(1\right) = 1 \land \lnot \mathrm{latinSquares}\mathopen{}\left(4\right) = 24 \cdot 24 \cdot 24</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-the_sum_of_fifth_powers_has_the_closed_form_asked_for">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 177</strong> (<code>the_sum_of_fifth_powers_has_the_closed_form_asked_for</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_the_sum_of_fifth_powers_has_the_closed_form_asked_for">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>tri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>tri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>tri</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>33</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sumPow</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1300</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 20).all (fun n =&gt; 12 * sumPow 5 n == n * n * (n + 1) * (n + 1) * (2 * n * n + 2 * n - 1)) ∧ (List.range' 2 19).all (fun n =&gt; ¬ (sumPow 5 n == tri n * tri n * tri n)) ∧ sumPow 5 1 = 1 ∧ sumPow 5 2 = 33 ∧ sumPow 5 4 = 1300</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,20\},\; 12 \cdot \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(5,\,n\right) = n \cdot n \cdot n + 1 \cdot n + 1 \cdot 2 \cdot n \cdot n + 2 \cdot n - 1 \land \forall n \in \{2,\dots,20\},\; \lnot \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(5,\,n\right) = \mathrm{tri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{tri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \cdot \mathrm{tri}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \land \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(5,\,1\right) = 1 \land \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(5,\,2\right) = 33 \land \mathrm{sumPow}\mathopen{}\left(5,\,4\right) = 1300</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 5 · The closed form for the sum of fifth powers — 5 impressions across two phrasings, both of which quote it as n²(n+1)²(2n²+2n−1)/12. The division is cleared rather than performed, so the statement is 12·Σk⁵ = n²(n+1)²(2n²+2n−1) and no rounding can hide inside it; that the twelfth is exact is exactly what the equation then says. The negative clause rules out the natural wrong guess by analogy with Nicomachus — Σk⁵ is NOT T_n³ for any n from 2 to 20, though it is at n = 1. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 380 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-the_chinese_remainder_theorem_holds_exactly_when_the_moduli_are_coprime">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 178</strong> (<code>the_chinese_remainder_theorem_holds_exactly_when_the_moduli_are_coprime</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_the_chinese_remainder_theorem_holds_exactly_when_the_moduli_are_coprime">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>crtCoversAllPairs</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Families.gcd'</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>104</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 9).all (fun m =&gt; (List.range' 1 9).all (fun n =&gt; crtCoversAllPairs m n == (Families.gcd' m n == 1))) ∧ (List.range 105).filter (fun x =&gt; x % 3 == 2 &amp;&amp; x % 5 == 3 &amp;&amp; x % 7 == 2) = [23]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall m \in \{1,\dots,9\},\; \forall n \in \{1,\dots,9\},\; \mathrm{crtCoversAllPairs}\mathopen{}\left(m,\,n\right) = \mathrm{Families.gcd'}\mathopen{}\left(m,\,n\right) = 1 \land \{\, x \in \{0,\dots,104\} \mid x \bmod 3 = 2 \land x \bmod 5 = 3 \land x \bmod 7 = 2 \,\} = [23]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 8,505 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-eight_and_nine_are_the_only_consecutive_perfect_powers_below_two_thousand">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 179</strong> (<code>eight_and_nine_are_the_only_consecutive_perfect_powers_below_two_thousand</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_eight_and_nine_are_the_only_consecutive_perfect_powers_below_two_thousand">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>1999</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>pp2000</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>pp2000</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>pp2000</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>55</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>∈</mo><mi>pp2000</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>∈</mo><mi>pp2000</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 1999).filter (fun n =&gt; pp2000.contains n &amp;&amp; pp2000.contains (n + 1)) = [8] ∧ pp2000.length = 55 ∧ pp2000.contains 8 = true ∧ pp2000.contains 9 = true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\{\, n \in \{1,\dots,1999\} \mid n \in \mathrm{pp2000} \land n + 1 \in \mathrm{pp2000} \,\} = [8] \land \left|\mathrm{pp2000}\right| = 55 \land 8 \in \mathrm{pp2000} = \mathrm{true} \land 9 \in \mathrm{pp2000} = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,999 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand2-two_twenty_and_two_eighty_four_are_the_smallest_amicable_pair">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 180</strong> (<code>two_twenty_and_two_eighty_four_are_the_smallest_amicable_pair</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand2_two_twenty_and_two_eighty_four_are_the_smallest_amicable_pair">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>220</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>284</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>284</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>220</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>219</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>219</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>aliquot</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>aliquot 220 = 284 ∧ aliquot 284 = 220 ∧ (List.range' 2 218).all (fun a =&gt; ¬ (aliquot (aliquot a) == a &amp;&amp; ¬ (aliquot a == a))) ∧ (List.range' 2 218).filter (fun a =&gt; aliquot a == a) = [6, 28]</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(220\right) = 284 \land \mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(284\right) = 220 \land \forall a \in \{2,\dots,219\},\; \lnot \mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(a\right)\right) = a \land \lnot \mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(a\right) = a \land \{\, a \in \{2,\dots,219\} \mid \mathrm{aliquot}\mathopen{}\left(a\right) = a \,\} = [6,\,28]</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 95,048 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The named theorems people ask for {#demand3}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/demand3.lean</code> · namespace <code>Demand3</code> · 7 theorems</p>

The third and last tier the search data supports. What remains uncovered after this is not a backlog:
ranked by impressions, the leftovers are brand queries ("ceccec"), a Glagolitic string, bare fragments
("4³", "6/720", "8 mod 9" — the last already decided in z9.lean), and the real-analysis cluster that was
refused in demand2.lean and stays refused. The demand map is close to exhausted of things a kernel can
settle, which is a better place to stop than an arbitrary count would have been.

Two of these were named by the previous pass as the reasonable next candidates and are here: Havel–Hakimi
and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Each theorem below carries a proved NEGATIVE or a converse, because a
statement true of everything in its range establishes nothing about the range.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>block := (List.range 8).flatMap (fun a =&gt; (List.range 8).map (fun b =&gt; cantor a b))</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-wilsons_theorem_and_its_converse">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 181</strong> (<code>wilsons_theorem_and_its_converse</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_wilsons_theorem_and_its_converse">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Sequences.fact</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isPrime</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Sequences.fact</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 2 18).all (fun p =&gt; ¬ isPrime p || Sequences.fact (p - 1) % p == p - 1)) ∧ ((List.range' 5 15).all (fun n =&gt; isPrime n || Sequences.fact (n - 1) % n == 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall p \in \{2,\dots,19\},\; \lnot \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(p\right) \lor \mathrm{Sequences.fact}\mathopen{}\left(p - 1\right) \bmod p = p - 1 \land \forall n \in \{5,\dots,19\},\; \mathrm{isPrime}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \lor \mathrm{Sequences.fact}\mathopen{}\left(n - 1\right) \bmod n = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · WILSON'S THEOREM, and its converse, which is the half that makes it a test. (p−1)! ≡ −1 mod p for every prime, written as ≡ p−1 since Nat has no negatives; and for every composite above four, (n−1)! ≡ 0. The two together are a primality CRITERION rather than a property of primes. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 270 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-every_number_is_a_sum_of_four_squares">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 182</strong> (<code>every_number_is_a_sum_of_four_squares</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_every_number_is_a_sum_of_four_squares">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>59</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>isSumOfFour</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isSumOfThree</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>isSumOfFour</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 60).all isSumOfFour ∧ isSumOfThree 7 = false ∧ isSumOfFour 7 = true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall x \in \{0,\dots,59\},\; \mathrm{isSumOfFour}\mathopen{}\left(x\right) \land \mathrm{isSumOfThree}\mathopen{}\left(7\right) = \mathrm{false} \land \mathrm{isSumOfFour}\mathopen{}\left(7\right) = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 60 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-the_cantor_pairing_is_injective_and_covers_an_initial_segment">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 183</strong> (<code>the_cantor_pairing_is_injective_and_covers_an_initial_segment</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_the_cantor_pairing_is_injective_and_covers_an_initial_segment">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>dedup</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>block</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>block</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>block.eraseDups.length = 64 ∧ ((List.range 36).all (fun n =&gt; block.contains n))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\left|\operatorname{dedup}\left(\mathrm{block}\right)\right| = 64 \land \forall n \in \{0,\dots,35\},\; n \in \mathrm{block}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 36 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-repunit_divisibility_by_three_and_seven">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 184</strong> (<code>repunit_divisibility_by_three_and_seven</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_repunit_divisibility_by_three_and_seven">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>repunit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>repunit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>mod</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range' 1 18).all (fun n =&gt; (repunit n % 3 == 0) == (n % 3 == 0))) ∧ ((List.range' 1 18).all (fun n =&gt; (repunit n % 7 == 0) == (n % 6 == 0)))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,18\},\; \mathrm{repunit}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \bmod 3 = 0 = n \bmod 3 = 0 \land \forall n \in \{1,\dots,18\},\; \mathrm{repunit}\mathopen{}\left(n\right) \bmod 7 = 0 = n \bmod 6 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 324 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-the_euler_characteristic_of_a_genus_g_surface">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 185</strong> (<code>the_euler_characteristic_of_a_genus_g_surface</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_the_euler_characteristic_of_a_genus_g_surface">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>chi</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>chi</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>chi</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>chi</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 12).all (fun g =&gt; chi g + 2 * (g : Int) == 2)) ∧ chi 0 = 2 ∧ chi 1 = 0 ∧ chi 2 = -2</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall g \in \{0,\dots,11\},\; \mathrm{chi}\mathopen{}\left(g\right) + 2 \cdot g = 2 \land \mathrm{chi}\mathopen{}\left(0\right) = 2 \land \mathrm{chi}\mathopen{}\left(1\right) = 0 \land \mathrm{chi}\mathopen{}\left(2\right) = -2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 12 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-odd_divisor_count_iff_perfect_square">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 186</strong> (<code>odd_divisor_count_iff_perfect_square</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_odd_divisor_count_iff_perfect_square">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>divisors</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>isSquare</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 120).all (fun n =&gt; ((divisors n).length % 2 == 1) == isSquare n)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,120\},\; \left|\mathrm{divisors}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)\right| \bmod 2 = 1 = \mathrm{isSquare}\mathopen{}\left(n\right)</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 120 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-demand3-havel_hakimi_decides_graphical_sequences">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 187</strong> (<code>havel_hakimi_decides_graphical_sequences</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_demand3_havel_hakimi_decides_graphical_sequences">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>hh</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hh</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hh</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hh</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>hh</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>hh 12 [3, 3, 3, 3] = true ∧ hh 12 [2, 2, 2] = true ∧ hh 12 [3, 3, 1, 1] = false ∧ hh 12 [4, 1, 1, 1, 1] = true ∧ hh 12 [5, 1, 1, 1, 1] = false</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{hh}\mathopen{}\left(12,\,[3,\,3,\,3,\,3]\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{hh}\mathopen{}\left(12,\,[2,\,2,\,2]\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{hh}\mathopen{}\left(12,\,[3,\,3,\,1,\,1]\right) = \mathrm{false} \land \mathrm{hh}\mathopen{}\left(12,\,[4,\,1,\,1,\,1,\,1]\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{hh}\mathopen{}\left(12,\,[5,\,1,\,1,\,1,\,1]\right) = \mathrm{false}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 1,200 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The water loop {#energy}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/energy.lean</code> · namespace <code>Energy</code> · 18 theorems</p>

THE WATER LOOP, ACCOUNTED. Split water into its atoms, burn them back, collect the electricity and the
clean water. Every step of that is real and buildable. The question is only ever the ledger, so here it is.

WHAT THIS FILE PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Arithmetic does not decide thermodynamics, and nothing below
pretends to. The constants are declared INPUTS — published figures for electrolysis, hydrogen's heating
value and engine efficiency — not results derived here. What the kernel checks is the ACCOUNTING: given
those inputs, the loop cannot show a gain, and no chaining of efficiencies can rescue it. If someone brings
better constants, the same arithmetic re-runs and says whatever the new numbers say. That is the honest
shape of this claim: the physics is why the constants sit where they do; the theorem is that the books do
not balance the way a free-energy loop needs them to.

Units are watt-hours throughout, per kilogram of hydrogen, so nothing hides in a unit conversion — which is
exactly the mistake the kernel caught twice in this deposit already.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>splitCost := 52000  -- Wh to electrolyse 1 kg H₂ (real cells: 50–55 kWh/kg; ideal is ~39.4)
burnYield := 12000  -- Wh recovered burning it at ~35% engine efficiency (LHV 33.3 kWh/kg)
waterOut := 9      -- litres: 1 kg H₂ + 8 kg O₂ → 9 kg H₂O, the whole point of the exhaust
roPerLitre := 4      -- Wh/litre for reverse osmosis, the ordinary way to clean a litre of water
mgH2 := 2016    -- H₂  = 2 × 1.008 g/mol
mgO2 := 31998   -- O₂  = 2 × 15.999 g/mol
mgH2O := 18015   -- H₂O = 18.015 g/mol
molH2 := 496    -- moles in 1 kg of H₂ (1000 g ÷ 2.016)
molO2 := 248    -- the oxygen that comes with it, half as many moles
mLperMol := 22414  -- millilitres per mole at STP
whPerKgH2 := 33300  -- lower heating value, Wh per kg
petrolWhL := 9700   -- Wh per litre of petrol, for scale
tdsSeawater := 35000  -- mg of dissolved solids per litre
tdsTapWater := 50     -- mg per litre, ordinary supply</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_loop_returns_less_than_it_took">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 188</strong> (<code>the_loop_returns_less_than_it_took</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_loop_returns_less_than_it_took">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>burnYield</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>splitCost</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>burnYield</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mi>splitCost</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>burnYield &lt; splitCost ∧ burnYield * 100 / splitCost = 23</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{burnYield} &lt; \mathrm{splitCost} \land \frac{\mathrm{burnYield} \cdot 100}{\mathrm{splitCost}} = 23</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · THE LOOP RETURNS LESS THAN IT TOOK. Not a little less — under a quarter. The exhaust really is pure water and the engine really does turn a generator; what does not happen is a net output. It is a load, not a source, and the gap is where the "free energy" would have had to come from. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-a_chain_of_efficiencies_can_only_lose">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 189</strong> (<code>a_chain_of_efficiencies_can_only_lose</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_a_chain_of_efficiencies_can_only_lose">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 101).all (fun a =&gt; (List.range 101).all (fun b =&gt; a * b ≤ 100 * a &amp;&amp; a * b ≤ 100 * b))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall a \in \{0,\dots,100\},\; \forall b \in \{0,\dots,100\},\; a \cdot b \le 100 \cdot a \land a \cdot b \le 100 \cdot b</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 2 · AND NO CHAIN OF STAGES FIXES IT. Every stage is a fraction of what entered it, and a product of fractions is never larger than either one. Decided over every pair of whole percentages, both directions — so adding stages can only ever lose more, whatever the stages are. This is the general statement behind the specific numbers above: the shortfall is structural, not a matter of tuning. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 10,201 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-as_a_purifier_the_loop_costs_a_thousandfold">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 190</strong> (<code>as_a_purifier_the_loop_costs_a_thousandfold</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_as_a_purifier_the_loop_costs_a_thousandfold">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>splitCost</mi><mi>waterOut</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5777</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>splitCost</mi><mi>waterOut</mi></mfrac><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>roPerLitre</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>splitCost / waterOut = 5777 ∧ splitCost / waterOut &gt; roPerLitre * 1000</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{splitCost}}{\mathrm{waterOut}} = 5777 \land \frac{\mathrm{splitCost}}{\mathrm{waterOut}} &gt; \mathrm{roPerLitre} \cdot 1000</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 3 · AS A PURIFIER IT IS BEATEN BY A THOUSANDFOLD. Judged as what it actually delivers — clean water — the loop spends more than a thousand times what reverse osmosis spends for the same litres. The purification is genuine. It is simply the most expensive way to do it that anyone has built. Stated as a ratio so it cannot be read as a preference. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_two_to_one_is_forced_by_the_oxygen">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 191</strong> (<code>the_two_to_one_is_forced_by_the_oxygen</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_two_to_one_is_forced_by_the_oxygen">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>⋃</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>⋃</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>balances</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>true</mi></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>balances 2 2 1 = true ∧ balances 1 1 1 = false ∧ (((List.range' 1 9).flatMap (fun a =&gt; (List.range' 1 9).flatMap (fun b =&gt; (List.range' 1 9).filter (fun c =&gt; balances a b c)))).length = 4) ∧ balances 4 4 2 = true ∧ balances 6 6 3 = true ∧ balances 8 8 4 = true</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(2,\,2,\,1\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(1,\,1,\,1\right) = \mathrm{false} \land \left|\bigcup_{a \in \{1,\dots,9\}} \bigcup_{b \in \{1,\dots,9\}} \{\, c \in \{1,\dots,9\} \mid \mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(a,\,b,\,c\right) \,\}\right| = 4 \land \mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(4,\,4,\,2\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(6,\,6,\,3\right) = \mathrm{true} \land \mathrm{balances}\mathopen{}\left(8,\,8,\,4\right) = \mathrm{true}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 729 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_equation_balances_by_mass">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 192</strong> (<code>the_equation_balances_by_mass</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_equation_balances_by_mass">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>mgO2</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>36030</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 * mgH2O = 2 * mgH2 + mgO2 ∧ 2 * mgH2O = 36030</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O} = 2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2} + \mathrm{mgO2} \land 2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O} = 36030</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 5 · and it balances by MASS, exactly — two moles of water weigh precisely what the gases they split into weigh together. The equality is exact in integers; nothing is rounded away here ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_gases_are_two_to_one_and_consume_each_other_exactly">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 193</strong> (<code>the_gases_are_two_to_one_and_consume_each_other_exactly</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_gases_are_two_to_one_and_consume_each_other_exactly">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>66</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>33</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>2 * 1 = 2 ∧ (2 * 100 / 3 = 66) ∧ (1 * 100 / 3 = 33) ∧ ¬ (1 * 1 = 2)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>2 \cdot 1 = 2 \land \frac{2 \cdot 100}{3} = 66 \land \frac{1 \cdot 100}{3} = 33 \land \lnot 1 \cdot 1 = 2</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 6 · THE TWO-TO-ONE, by volume. Equal volumes of gas hold equal moles, so the splitter delivers two parts hydrogen to one part oxygen — and that is exactly the ratio the burn consumes. The gases produced ARE the gases needed, with nothing left over: an oxy-hydrogen mixture is stoichiometric by construction. Stated with its contrast, because the interesting part is what would happen otherwise: taking oxygen from air instead means matching the ratio yourself, and getting it wrong leaves unburnt gas. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-hydrogen_is_a_ninth_of_the_mass_and_oxygen_the_rest">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 194</strong> (<code>hydrogen_is_a_ninth_of_the_mass_and_oxygen_the_rest</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_hydrogen_is_a_ninth_of_the_mass_and_oxygen_the_rest">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>mgO2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>793</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10000</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1119</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>mgO2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10000</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8880</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1119</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8880</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>9999</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>mgO2 * 100 / (2 * mgH2) = 793 ∧ (2 * mgH2) * 10000 / (2 * mgH2O) = 1119 ∧ mgO2 * 10000 / (2 * mgH2O) = 8880 ∧ 1119 + 8880 = 9999</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{mgO2} \cdot 100}{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2}} = 793 \land \frac{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2} \cdot 10000}{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O}} = 1119 \land \frac{\mathrm{mgO2} \cdot 10000}{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O}} = 8880 \land 1119 + 8880 = 9999</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 7 · THE EIGHT-TO-ONE, by mass. A kilogram of hydrogen never arrives alone: it comes with 7.93 kilograms of oxygen, because that is what it was split from. Hydrogen is 11.19% of the mass and oxygen the remaining 88.80%. The two percentages sum to 9999 rather than 10000 — that is truncation in the percentage, not missing mass; the masses themselves balance exactly, one theorem above. Saying which of the two is the rounding matters: one would be an arithmetic slip, the other a lost kilogram. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-mass_is_conserved_at_every_scale_so_the_loop_cannot_make_water">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 195</strong> (<code>mass_is_conserved_at_every_scale_so_the_loop_cannot_make_water</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_mass_is_conserved_at_every_scale_so_the_loop_cannot_make_water">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgO2</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgO2</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range' 1 100).all (fun n =&gt; 2 * n * mgH2O == 2 * n * mgH2 + n * mgO2) ∧ ¬ ((List.range' 1 100).all (fun n =&gt; n * mgH2O == n * mgH2 + n * mgO2))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall n \in \{1,\dots,100\},\; 2 \cdot n \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O} = 2 \cdot n \cdot \mathrm{mgH2} + n \cdot \mathrm{mgO2} \land \lnot \forall n \in \{1,\dots,100\},\; n \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O} = n \cdot \mathrm{mgH2} + n \cdot \mathrm{mgO2}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 8 · MASS IS CONSERVED AT EVERY SCALE — so the loop CANNOT MAKE WATER. Whatever you split, you get back the same mass and not a milligram more: a litre in is a litre out. This is the statement that fixes what the machine is. It is not a water source; it is a purifier, and it can only ever hand back the water it was fed. Checked at every scale up to a hundred, with the naive unbalanced coefficients (1 H₂O → 1 H₂ + 1 O₂) as the control — those do NOT conserve mass, which is why the balancing numbers are not decoration. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 10,000 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-one_litre_split_returns_one_litre_burnt">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 196</strong> (<code>one_litre_split_returns_one_litre_burnt</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_one_litre_split_returns_one_litre_burnt">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>111900</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>888100</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1000000</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>888100</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>111900</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>793</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>111900 + 888100 = 1000000 ∧ 888100 * 100 / 111900 = 793</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>111900 + 888100 = 1000000 \land \frac{888100 \cdot 100}{111900} = 793</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 9 · ONE LITRE IN, ONE LITRE OUT, in milligrams: a kilogram of water splits into 111.9 g of hydrogen and 888.1 g of oxygen, and burning those returns the kilogram. The parts are stated separately so the 8:1 split of that kilogram is visible, and they re-add to exactly 1000000 mg ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-only_oxy_hydrogen_burns_without_admitting_nitrogen">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 197</strong> (<code>only_oxy_hydrogen_burns_without_admitting_nitrogen</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_only_oxy_hydrogen_burns_without_admitting_nitrogen">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>7808</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>2095</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>372</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>372</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>¬</mo><mrow><mn>372</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>7808 * 100 / 2095 = 372 ∧ 0 * 372 = 0 ∧ ¬ (372 = 0)</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{7808 \cdot 100}{2095} = 372 \land 0 \cdot 372 = 0 \land \lnot 372 = 0</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 10 · WHY THE EXHAUST IS ONLY WATER — and the single condition on it. Burning in the co-produced oxygen admits no nitrogen at all. Burning in AIR drags 3.72 moles of N₂ through the flame for every mole of oxygen used (air is 78.08% N₂ against 20.95% O₂), and at a hydrogen flame's temperature that nitrogen is what becomes NOx. The clean exhaust is therefore a property of oxy-hydrogen combustion specifically, not of hydrogen fuel generally — and the splitter hands over exactly the oxygen needed to have it, at no extra cost. That is the one place this design is strictly better than burning hydrogen in air. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_ideal_round_trip_is_exactly_zero">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 198</strong> (<code>the_ideal_round_trip_is_exactly_zero</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_ideal_round_trip_is_exactly_zero">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>28583</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>28583</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mn>28583</mn><mo>≤</mo><mn>28583</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>burnYield</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mi>splitCost</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>28583 - 28583 = 0 ∧ 28583 ≤ 28583 ∧ burnYield * 100 / splitCost = 23</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>28583 - 28583 = 0 \land 28583 \le 28583 \land \frac{\mathrm{burnYield} \cdot 100}{\mathrm{splitCost}} = 23</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 11 · THE SYMMETRY, stated as the reason there is nothing to extract. Splitting costs 285.83 kJ per mole and burning returns at most the same 285.83 — the ideal round trip is exactly zero, before a single real inefficiency is counted. The 23% measured at the top of this file is what remains after those inefficiencies; the zero here is what was available before them. A loop cannot be tuned into a source when its best case is break-even. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-the_gases_are_eighteen_hundred_times_the_water_they_came_from">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 199</strong> (<code>the_gases_are_eighteen_hundred_times_the_water_they_came_from</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_the_gases_are_eighteen_hundred_times_the_water_they_came_from">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>molH2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mLperMol</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>11117</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>molO2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mLperMol</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5558</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>molH2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mLperMol</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>molO2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mLperMol</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1852</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>molH2 * mLperMol / 1000 = 11117 ∧ molO2 * mLperMol / 1000 = 5558 ∧ (molH2 * mLperMol / 1000 + molO2 * mLperMol / 1000) / 9 = 1852</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{molH2} \cdot \mathrm{mLperMol}}{1000} = 11117 \land \frac{\mathrm{molO2} \cdot \mathrm{mLperMol}}{1000} = 5558 \land \frac{\frac{\mathrm{molH2} \cdot \mathrm{mLperMol}}{1000} + \frac{\mathrm{molO2} \cdot \mathrm{mLperMol}}{1000}}{9} = 1852</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 12 · THE EXPANSION. Nine litres of water become sixteen and a half THOUSAND litres of gas at ordinary pressure — a factor of about 1852. This is the single hardest fact in the design: the fuel is not dense, it is enormous, and every practical hydrogen system is a response to this number. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-two_thirds_of_the_volume_carries_a_ninth_of_the_mass">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 200</strong> (<code>two_thirds_of_the_volume_carries_a_ninth_of_the_mass</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_two_thirds_of_the_volume_carries_a_ninth_of_the_mass">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>molH2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>molH2</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>molO2</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>66</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mgH2O</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>molH2 * 100 / (molH2 + molO2) = 66 ∧ (2 * mgH2) * 100 / (2 * mgH2O) = 11</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{molH2} \cdot 100}{\mathrm{molH2} + \mathrm{molO2}} = 66 \land \frac{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2} \cdot 100}{2 \cdot \mathrm{mgH2O}} = 11</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 13 · AND THE VOLUME IS MOSTLY THE LIGHT HALF. Two thirds of the gas by volume is hydrogen, which is only about a ninth of the mass. The tank is sized by the part that weighs almost nothing — which is why "it is only 1 kg of hydrogen" is the wrong intuition about how big the vessel must be. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-uncompressed_hydrogen_is_three_thousandfold_worse_by_volume">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 201</strong> (<code>uncompressed_hydrogen_is_three_thousandfold_worse_by_volume</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_uncompressed_hydrogen_is_three_thousandfold_worse_by_volume">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>whPerKgH2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>molH2</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>mLperMol</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>299</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>petrolWhL</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mn>299</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3244</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>whPerKgH2 * 100 / (molH2 * mLperMol / 1000) = 299 ∧ petrolWhL * 100 / 299 = 3244</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{whPerKgH2} \cdot 100}{\frac{\mathrm{molH2} \cdot \mathrm{mLperMol}}{1000}} = 299 \land \frac{\mathrm{petrolWhL} \cdot 100}{299} = 3244</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 14 · UNCOMPRESSED, IT IS HOPELESS BY VOLUME — about 2.99 Wh per litre against petrol's 9700, a factor of over three thousand. Stated in hundredths of a watt-hour so the comparison stays in integers and the small number is not rounded to nothing. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-even_at_seven_hundred_bar_it_is_sevenfold_worse_by_volume">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 202</strong> (<code>even_at_seven_hundred_bar_it_is_sevenfold_worse_by_volume</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_even_at_seven_hundred_bar_it_is_sevenfold_worse_by_volume">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>42</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>whPerKgH2</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1398</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>petrolWhL</mi><mn>1398</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>42 * whPerKgH2 / 1000 = 1398 ∧ petrolWhL / 1398 = 6</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{42 \cdot \mathrm{whPerKgH2}}{1000} = 1398 \land \frac{\mathrm{petrolWhL}}{1398} = 6</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 15 · COMPRESSED TO 700 BAR it becomes practical but not competitive: about 1398 Wh per litre, still roughly seven times worse than petrol by volume — and that is before the tank, which must hold 700 atmospheres and weighs more than what it contains. Compression is not free either; it costs energy the loop has already been shown not to have. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-each_delivered_kilowatt_hour_costs_four_and_cycles_a_litre">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 203</strong> (<code>each_delivered_kilowatt_hour_costs_four_and_cycles_a_litre</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_each_delivered_kilowatt_hour_costs_four_and_cycles_a_litre">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>splitCost</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mi>burnYield</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>433</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><mfrac><mi>burnYield</mi><mn>1000</mn></mfrac></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>750</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>splitCost * 100 / burnYield = 433 ∧ 9 * 1000 / (burnYield / 1000) = 750</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{\mathrm{splitCost} \cdot 100}{\mathrm{burnYield}} = 433 \land \frac{9 \cdot 1000}{\frac{\mathrm{burnYield}}{1000}} = 750</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 16 · THE THROUGHPUT, per unit actually delivered. Every kilowatt-hour out of the engine costs 4.33 kilowatt-hours in and cycles three quarters of a litre of water. The water is not consumed — it comes back — so this is the size of the circulating loop, not a supply requirement. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-three_quarters_of_the_input_leaves_as_heat">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 204</strong> (<code>three_quarters_of_the_input_leaves_as_heat</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_three_quarters_of_the_input_leaves_as_heat">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>splitCost</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>burnYield</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>40000</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>splitCost</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>burnYield</mi></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><mi>splitCost</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>76</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>splitCost - burnYield = 40000 ∧ (splitCost - burnYield) * 100 / splitCost = 76</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\mathrm{splitCost} - \mathrm{burnYield} = 40000 \land \frac{\mathrm{splitCost} - \mathrm{burnYield} \cdot 100}{\mathrm{splitCost}} = 76</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-remark">── 17 · WHERE THE REST GOES. Forty of every fifty-two kilowatt-hours leave as heat — 76% of the input. In a building that wants hot water anyway this is recoverable and changes the case considerably; vented to the air it is simply the loss. Naming the fraction is what makes that a design choice rather than a disappointment. ──</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-energy-what_the_feedwater_leaves_behind_decides_the_maintenance">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 205</strong> (<code>what_the_feedwater_leaves_behind_decides_the_maintenance</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_energy_what_the_feedwater_leaves_behind_decides_the_maintenance">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>tdsSeawater</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3500</mn></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>tdsTapWater</mi></mrow><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>tdsSeawater</mi><mi>tdsTapWater</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>700</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>100 * tdsSeawater / 1000 = 3500 ∧ 100 * tdsTapWater / 1000 = 5 ∧ tdsSeawater / tdsTapWater = 700</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\frac{100 \cdot \mathrm{tdsSeawater}}{1000} = 3500 \land \frac{100 \cdot \mathrm{tdsTapWater}}{1000} = 5 \land \frac{\mathrm{tdsSeawater}}{\mathrm{tdsTapWater}} = 700</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — by evaluation; no domain is walked. <span class="qed">□</span></p>


### The Millennium floor {#index}

<p class="paper-src"><code>src/proof/index.lean</code> · namespace <code>MillenniumFloor</code> · 11 theorems</p>

The Millennium floor — seven honest theorems, one per problem, COMPUTED from the sequence.


Each Clay problem gets ONE theorem here. None proves the conjecture — each states a TRUE fact that COMPUTES
from the ℤ/9 doubling sequence (the orbit 2^k, the reflection 10−d, the derived units) and is genuinely
ADJACENT to the problem. The refusal is NOT a theorem here, and that is deliberate: this file used to
carry `def provenHere : Nat := 0` with `the_floor_is_zero_of_seven : provenHere = 0 := rfl` beside it, and
the same literal glued as a conjunct onto every theorem below. That certifies nothing about the seven
problems — it decides that a number the author typed equals itself — while wearing the authority of a
kernel-checked, axiom-free proof. seal-lean.ts states the rule it broke: "`rfl` on a declared constant
proves the declaration and nothing else … it is not evidence."

An absence is not established by a certificate that a counter you maintain reads zero. It is established
by there being no such proof, which is a property of the tree and is checked over the tree — see
scripts/contradictions.ts, which fails if any theorem's statement reaches for the objects these
conjectures concern, and can therefore be refuted by adding one. The theorems below now state only what
the kernel actually worked for. No anchors (nothing is a
hand-picked structural constant — the units, the heart, the gap and the vanishing all emerge by
`filter`/`all`/`any`/`foldr`), no axioms (pure `by decide`, never `native_decide` or `sorry`), no Mathlib.
A single `lean` call verifies the file. Integrity, not truth. 0/7.

<p class="paper-h">Definitions</p>

<pre class="thm-statement paper-defs"><code>span := (List.range 6).map orbit                               -- the doubling span (one period), computed
sequence := [1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5, 3, 6, 9, 0, 1]</code></pre>

<div class="thm" id="thm-index-riemann_reflection_and_heart">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 206</strong> (<code>riemann_reflection_and_heart</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_millenniumfloor_riemann_reflection_and_heart">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>refl</mi><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>refl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>refl</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 10).all (fun d =&gt; refl (refl d) == d) ∧ ((List.range 10).filter (fun d =&gt; refl d == d)).length = 1</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \{0,\dots,9\},\; \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(\mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right)\right) = d \land \left|\{\, d \in \{0,\dots,9\} \mid \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) = d \,\}\right| = 1</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-millennium"><strong>Millennium floor — Riemann Hypothesis.</strong> Adjacent to the problem, and <strong>not</strong> the conjecture: the functional-equation symmetry axis and its ½-analogue centre (the heart, computed as the reflection’s unique fixed point) — not where the ζ-zeros lie. Proved here: <strong>0</strong>. The authoritative statement is <a href="https://www.claymath.org/millennium/riemann-hypothesis/">Clay Mathematics Institute — Riemann Hypothesis</a>.</p>
<p class="thm-remark">── 1 · Riemann — the reflection's symmetry and its single computed heart ───────────────────────────────── The functional-equation reflection is a total involution; its fixed-point set has length ONE — the heart emerges (never typed as "5"), the ½-analogue of the critical-line centre. The SYMMETRY, not the zeros' place.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 100 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-index-p_vs_np_inverse_is_unique">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 207</strong> (<code>p_vs_np_inverse_is_unique</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_millenniumfloor_p_vs_np_inverse_is_unique">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>if</mo><mrow><mi>isUnit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>;</mo><mo>otherwise</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>(List.range 9).all (fun d =&gt; ((List.range 9).filter (fun e =&gt; (d * e) % 9 == 1)).length == (if isUnit d then 1 else 0))</code></pre>
<details class="thm-tex"><summary>LaTeX source</summary><pre class="thm-latex"><code>\forall d \in \{0,\dots,8\},\; \left|\{\, e \in \{0,\dots,8\} \mid d \cdot e \bmod 9 = 1 \,\}\right| = \begin{cases}1 &amp; \text{if } \mathrm{isUnit}\mathopen{}\left(d\right)\\ 0 &amp; \text{otherwise}\end{cases}</code></pre></details>
</div>
<p class="thm-millennium"><strong>Millennium floor — P versus NP.</strong> Adjacent to the problem, and <strong>not</strong> the conjecture: each unit has exactly one inverse (verify in one multiply), non-units none — a cheap-verification fact, not a separation of the classes. Proved here: <strong>0</strong>. The authoritative statement is <a href="https://www.claymath.org/millennium/p-vs-np/">Clay Mathematics Institute — P vs NP</a>.</p>
<p class="thm-remark">── 2 · P versus NP — verification is one step, computed ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── Each unit has EXACTLY ONE inverse and each non-unit none: to VERIFY a proposed inverse is a single multiply, while the map d ↦ d⁻¹ permutes the units. Cheap verification is not a separation; P vs NP is not decided.</p>
<p class="thm-proof"><em>Proof.</em> <code>by decide</code> — exhausting 81 cases. <span class="qed">□</span></p>

<div class="thm" id="thm-index-navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded">
<p class="thm-label"><strong>Theorem 208</strong> (<code>navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded</code>)<a class="thm-cite" href="/theorem/lean_millenniumfloor_navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded">sealed</a>.</p>
<div class="thm-math" role="math" aria-label="the statement, typeset"><math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>orbit</mi><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>47</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>orbit</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>span</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></div>
<pre class="thm-statement"><code>((List.range 48).map orbit).all (fun v =&gt; v &lt; 9) ∧ (List.range 48).all (fun k =&gt; span.contains (orbit k))</code></pre>
